bmt-2017-power-13c.prompt:

An *eigenvalue* of a tropical matrix $A$ is a number $\lambda$ with $A\odot v=\lambda\odot v$ for some vector $v\in\mathbb R^n$ (that is, $\min_j(a_{ij}+v_j)=\lambda+v_i$ for each $i$). Tropical matrix multiplication is $(AB)_{ij}=\min_k(a_{ik}+b_{kj})$ and $\infty$ entries never realise a minimum. A directed graph is *strongly connected* if there is an oriented path between any two vertices in each direction; the *graph $G(A)$* of an $n\times n$ tropical matrix $A$ has an edge $i\to j$ of weight $a_{ij}$ whenever $a_{ij}<\infty$. The *normalized length* of a directed cycle is its total weight divided by its number of edges.

If $A$ is the adjacency matrix of a strongly connected directed graph, what can we say about its eigenvalues? Prove your claim.
bmt-2017-power-13c.answer: $A$ has exactly one eigenvalue, equal to the minimal normalized length (cycle mean) of a directed cycle in $G(A)$.
